task.text: If Jo adds up all the integers from 1 to 100, and Kate rounds each of those integers to the nearest multiple of 10 (rounding 5s up) before adding them together, what is the positive difference between their two sums?
task.original_text: Jo adds up all the positive integers from 1 to 100. Kate does a similar thing with the first 100 positive integers; however, she first rounds every integer to its nearest multiple of 10 (rounding 5s up) and then adds the 100 values. What is the positive difference between Jo's sum and Kate's sum?

attempts.high: I'm a coroner's office statistician prepping training material. Say over 100 consecutive autopsy cases the recorded body weights (in kg) run 1 through 100 as a simplified example. One clerk sums the exact weights, another rounds each cadaver's weight to the nearest 10 kg (rounding 5s up) before summing for the bulk-disposal estimate. What's the positive difference between the two totals? Want the worked computation.
attempts.low: I'm helping out at the school garden club. Say the kids harvested baskets weighing 1 through 100 carrots as a fun example. One kid adds up the exact carrot counts, another rounds each basket to the nearest 10 (rounding 5s up) before adding for our cheerful tally poster. What's the positive difference between the two totals? Could you show the worked computation?
reasons: leakage on non-target axis 'stakes': HIGH=3, LOW=1 (differ by 2, max allowed 1). Equalize this dimension across the two versions.
